bio:
Samuel Thompson was born on 4 March 1668, the youngest son of John Thompson of Setauket, John's 11th-great-grandfather, and so a brother of John's 10th-great-grandmother Elizabeth (Thompson) Smith. A farmer at Setauket, he married on 6 November 1709 and made his will on 3 April 1745. His children were Jonathan, Isaac, who was lost at sea about 1735, Susannah, who married Thomas Strong, Mary, who married Daniel Smith, Deborah, who married Arthur Smith and then William Miller, Ruth, who married Thomas Telford, and Sarah. His silver tankard passed to the grandson whose son became the historian of Long Island.

He died at Setauket on 14 July 1749 and was buried at the Setauket Presbyterian Church, in the south-east corner of the churchyard, where part of his tombstone still survived in 1918.
sources: [R4-S1] B. F. Thompson, History of Long Island, 3rd ed. (1918), vol. 3 (archive.org full text), pp. 296-297 (secondary) https://archive.org/details/historyoflongisl003thom
